16 A car of total mass 1560 kg is travelling with a constant speed of 32 m s–1. The driving force
provided by the car is 680 N. The kinetic energy of the car is 800 kJ and its momentum is
50 000 N s.
Which two items of data could be used to calculate the useful power output of the car?
A
driving force and momentum
B
kinetic energy and mass
C
mass and momentum
D
speed and driving force

hints: Notice the wording constant speed of 32 $\text{m s}^{-1}$ with driving force 680 $\text{N}$ - the speed is not changing so kinetic energy stays at 800 $\text{kJ}$.
Recall the power relation for a force moving its point of application: $P = Fv$ for force parallel to velocity.
Check which pair in the options supplies both $F$ in $\text{N}$ and $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ at the same instant, without needing time or extra steps.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: driving force $F = 680$ $\text{N}$ and constant speed $v = 32$ $\text{m s}^{-1}$ for the 1560 kg car.
State the governing rule for mechanical power: power is the rate of doing work, $P = \frac{F\Delta x}{\Delta t} = Fv$ when $F$ and $v$ are parallel.
Substitute the values with units: $P = 680 \times 32$ with units $\text{N} \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{W}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $P = 21760$ $\text{W}$, about 22 $\text{kW}$, confirming the units give watts.
Stored kinetic energy of 800 $\text{kJ}$ and momentum of 50 000 $\text{N s}$ do not give a rate unless a time is known, and mass alone does not give power.
Only the speed and driving force pair provides $F$ and $v$ for $P = Fv$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Momentum $p = mv$ can give speed if mass is known, but driving force and momentum alone do not give $P = Fv$ without first finding $v$.

B.explanation: Kinetic energy and mass give speed from $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$, but they do not include the 680 N driving force needed for $P = Fv$.

C.explanation: Mass and momentum give speed from $v = p/m$, but they do not include the driving force so useful power cannot be found directly.

D.explanation: Useful power at constant speed is $P = Fv$, so the 680 N driving force and 32 $\text{m s}^{-1}$ speed give power directly.
